question.worked_solution:
First, we isolate the term with the variable exponent by dividing both sides by $3$:

$$
\begin{aligned}3\cdot {5}^{s} & =75 \\ \frac{3\cdot {5}^{s}}{3} & =\frac{75}{3} \\ {5}^{s} & =25\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we rewrite $25$ as ${5}^{2}$ to get:

$$
\begin{aligned}{5}^{s} & =25 \\ {5}^{s} & ={5}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since both sides of the equation share the same base $(5)$, we equate the exponents:

$$
\begin{aligned}{5}^{s} & ={5}^{2} \\ s & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $s=2.$
